notes.title: Workshop at least!
notes.content:
Hello!

I just released a patch with some gameplay fixes and two great features.

[h2]Gameplay Fixes[/h2]

-Bandit leaders can now personally lead an army.
This changes a lot of things, so let me know if it feels unbalanced.

-Recruiting for an army with a sufficiently large stock of guns will no longer deplete the faction’s gun stock.

I also killed tons of minor bugs you don’t even need to hear about.


[h2]The Workshop is Open![/h2]

You can find the documentation for it here: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3456566337

At the moment, only two editor tools are available:

A translation tool to provide better text in your language.

A character editor to create and maintain mods like "Moe of the White Sun."

This feature was a lot of hard work, and consider it a test for more editor tools.
My ambition is that one day, you’ll be able to edit entire scenarios with their own dialogues.
So, your feedback is crucial.

Please: if you break the game while tinkering with its files, read the Steam guide I made before reaching out to me. The solution may already be available.

[h2]My Latest Game is Out![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/e0054a620c019244eb8ef6551dd88d4aa4a046d8.jpg[/img]

The game is available in English, French, and Chinese (even though the store might not say so).
It’s an easy-to-pick-up but highly replayable Cold War 2 strategy game.
It’s available at the bargain price of $4.99, so if you want to support an indie dev while enjoying hours of fun with a great game, just get it now!
You can find it here: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3204120/Maestros_Cold_War_2/

Do you know what’s so great about this news?

I can now focus again on the Rise of the White Sun DLC!
(By the way, the editor tools will let players get a sneak peek at the future characters and event texts.)

I hope you’ll be able to unleash your creativity with the new tools!

Maestro Cinetik

notes.title: Quality of Life & UI 2025 Update and Korean Localization
notes.content:
Hello!

This new update focuses on players quality of life with some screen interractions reworked.
Also: Korean language has also been added to the game, thanks to the community.

[b]Wh'os Who windows[/b]
The who's who window is now more practical, and will display more informations.
You can now manage more things from the who's who, like recruiting characters or delegating them to the AI.
A faction tooltip has been added, and you can jump directly on that faction's diplomatic screen by clicking on the faction icon.
Once a character has been selected in the who's who, it is now easy to inspect all other characters from that faction, thanks to the side arrows I added.

[b]Diplomacy and government panel[/b]
The navigation has been simplified, and factions tooltips added everywhere.

[b]Districts management screen[/b]
Hovering the faction flag will now display a tooltip, so you don't have to click the flag to get more informations.

[b]Army screen[/b]
I added the same faction tooltip as everywhere, and you can now jump right into a unit faction's window by clicking on the unit icon.

[b]Province screen[/b]
(that's the screen you access from the left button on the map view)
I added more informations on characters, like the origine province and if they are southerners or northerners.

[b]End turn reports[/b]
The end turn reports panel will now automatically pop up at each new turn.
That festures has been requested several times, and now you have it!
If like me, it annoys you, you can simply descativate that feature from the options menu.

I hope this update will make things more simple for new players not familar with the warlord era.

Have fun!  

PS: If you want to see what I am working on these days, there is a demo available containing 6 scenarios.
It is a strategy game about the cold war, much more easy to play than Rise of the White Sun.
The demo can be found here: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3361850/Maestros_Cold_War_2_Demo/

notes.title: The 6th Congress
notes.content:
As you may know, I am working on an exciting 1929-1933 DLC. While it is quite a heavy workload, I won’t keep you waiting too long for new content—I will ship smaller updates like this one from time to time!

[h2]The 6th Congress Content Update[/h2]

This update brings new content to the 1927 Red Bases scenario:
[list]
[*] 2 new events related to the 6th Congress of the Communist Party
[*] 2 new Communist Characters (they enter the game after the 6th congress)
[*] 5 new actions to developp your Red Bases!
[*] A reworked AI for the Guomindang in this particular scenario
[*] New historical portraits for Liu Xing(刘铏) and Zang Zhiping
[*] 2 new cheat codes
[*] 4 new achievements
[/list]

In July 1928, the Communist Party gathered in Moscow to discuss the aftermath of the breakdown of the First United Front between the CCP and the Kuomintang.
A new direction was set, and this is reflected in the new actions available for the Communist factions to develop their districts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/58fdd338fbfbd9ff789c5e492c44caa9f7b6784e.png[/img]

[h3]The new actions are:[/h3]

[u][b]Red Base[/b][/u]
The Party begins the process of establishing executive committees in every district, town, and village. These committees are tasked with assisting in the creation of soviets by local assemblies.
This endeavor is far from straightforward. 
Not only does the population harbor fears of a resurgence of the Guomindang or warlord troops, but it is also challenging to find competent locals who fully grasp the new organizational structure.
To overcome these obstacles, the Party must rely on the support of local associations to continuously communicate and clarify its actions.
There are no shortcuts: achieving transformation into a genuine Red base, backed by the people, demands persistent and audacious political effort.
==>Upon the successful implementation of this policy, your influence across all social classes will rise by 10, while the influence of other factions will diminish by 20.
==>Additionally, Peasant Self-Defense Corps summoned in this district will be reinforced with more members, and recruitment actions will be more efficient.

[u][b]Young vanguard[/b][/u]
Young men from this district are organized into young vanguard units. 
In the event of a crisis, the regular army will be supported by these groups, who are intimately familiar with the terrain. 
Tasks such as scouting enemy movements, supplying the army, and securing the rear can confidently be entrusted to these enthusiastic vanguard groups.
==>Upon the completion of this policy, the Peasant Defense Corps summoned in this district will have higher morale, and enemy troops will face a higher chance of being ambushed.
==>Enemies in this district are automatically spied upon

[u][b]Land Refrom[/b][/u]
Land Reform is a critically necessary policy, yet lessons have been learned from past local, clumsy attempts: it is now understood that rallying all peasants into a broad front is essential. 
While leadership of the peasant associations must be entrusted to the poor peasants, it is crucial not to alienate the medium peasants. 
Consequently, land redistribution must be carried out judiciously, with a keen consideration of local conditions, especially in areas where medium peasants predominate.
==>Your influence over the gentry and the merchants will immediately decrease by 50.
==>Vitality and Tradition will decrease by 20, as disrupting traditional structures inevitably leads to some short-term troubles.
==>Upon the completion of this policy, your influence over peasants will increase by 20, and the influence of other factions will decrease by 20.
==>Agriculture income will be increased by 10%
==>Every Peasant leaders in this province will gain 25 Face and 25 supporters.

[u][b]Model Villages[/b][/u]
Establishing Model villages to conduct political and agricultural experiments will enhance the prospects of long-term success for the Land Reform.
This is an occasion to test bottom-up methods of policy development through consultation with locals, to adopt their practical suggestions while reserving broader policy questions to the Party's evaluation. Insights gained from these model villages can be extensively disseminated, benefiting the entire province.
Upon completion, this policy will:
==>Increase vitality and agriculture income by 5.
==>Decrease Tradition by 1 in all districts of this province with a soviet.

[u][b]Anti-Opium Campaign[/b][/u]
Opium fields are destroyed and alternative crops promoted.
Strict penalties awaits those involved in the opium trade.
Educational rallies are organized in the villages and rehabilitation programs to treat addicts are set up, emphasizing both medical care and ideological education.
These efforts aimed to eliminate opium's harmful effects and promote a drug-free society gained a large approval among the population.
==>You gain 50 Face
==>Opium income is reduced to zero.
==>Upon completion, the vitality and the base agricultural income will increase by 5, and the population will lose its addiction to opium.

[h3]The new cheat codes are:[/h3]
The 6th congress is late in the regular 1927 Red Bases scenario, and you may not have that much time to test all the new actions.
The solution is either to play the Sandbox mode, either to use these cheat codes:

"6thcongress": will unlock the advanced actions, you can use it in any scenario.

"NanchangRedBase": will have the same effect but will also create a soviet, a red base and complete a land reform in Nanchang.

[h3]New achievements[/h3]

I’ve added one achievement for each of the Communist groups in the 1927 Red Bases scenario.

I hope you will like this new update.

Have fun!

Maestro Cinetik

notes.title: Famine Relief Update
notes.content:
The latest patch includes:

[list]
[*]5 new actions related to drought and famine management.
[*]A reworked 1920 AI, enhancing the defense of Shanghai.
[/list]
 
[b]New Famine Relief Actions[/b]

Responding to your requests for more options to combat drought, I've introduced 5 new district policies and actions. Most of these actions incur an upkeep cost and are unlocked via the Chamber of Commerce upgrade.

[u]Temporary Relief Societies[/u]: Officials and philanthropists will participate in this initiative, undertaking charity and relief efforts. This policy will unlock additional options and reduce the number of bandits generated by drought.

[u]Discounted Sales Granaries[/u]: An effective method to supply the district with grain and manage prices. These granaries will reduce the duration of droughts each turn and help restore vitality if it has dropped too low. Like the Temporary Relief Societies, these granaries also reduce the number of bandits created by drought.

[u]Soup Kitchens[/u]: Easier to set up than granaries, they will reduce the duration of famine, albeit with lower efficiency and maintenance costs.

[u]Dragon King Rituals[/u]: In the game, when the population implores the Dragon King for rain, it never works. However, this action will increase your Face (reputation), tradition, and influence over peasants.

[u]Speculate on Grain[/u]: Another action that allows for quick, albeit unethical, earnings by exploiting a district's resources.

Another great change is that from time to time, private initiative will provide relief to a district in distress.

[b]1920 AI Reworked[/b]

The AI in the 1920 scenario was ineffective at defending Shanghai. With this rework, the AI will now be more proactive and strategic in its defense.

[b]What's Next?[/b]

I have started coding for the 1929-1932 DLC. While I cannot provide a release date yet, progress is underway.

Enjoy the game!

Maestro Cinetik

notes.title: The Yellow Way - New (free) DLC
notes.content:
Hello!

I have been frantically patching the game recently to improve the quality of life, add new features, and release a free DLC. I hope you will be as satisfied with the result as I am!

[h2]The Yellow Way (Free DLC)[/h2]

This DLC unlocks a new faction in the Little Model China and 1920 Sandboxes. The Yellow Way society is very similar to the later Heavenly Gate Society, but its victory conditions are designed for bolder players.

In Henan, drought, floods, and banditry have led to a resurgence of secret society activities. Near Anyang, an alliance between a Yellow Way master and a mysterious man claiming to be a ninth-generation descendant of the Ming dynasty has sparked an outright rebellion against the Republic.

The rebels aim to restore the Ming Dynasty!

Though underarmed, their ranks are rapidly growing, and they are now able to besiege local garrisons. The rebels know the area well and have so far resisted all attempts by the authorities to take them down.

Why a free DLC instead of just new content for the game?

Two reasons:

-I made this faction stronger than it was historically for the sake of fun, so it does not entirely fit into the original game.
-I am experimenting with Steam DLCs for the future development of the game.

[h2]Quality of Life Improvements[/h2]

*I reworked the "Escape" navigate back feature so it now works as players expect.
*I fixed some issues that used to slow the game.
*I added some useful tooltips when you hover over armies on the map.

I plan to keep adding quality of life features between major content updates. Also, check the options menu—there are settings that may significantly improve your experience!

[h2]Achievements![/h2]

I realize now how silly it was to add them so late in the game's life, but here they are. ^^

I will continue adding achievements from time to time as completion scores rise.

Enjoy!

Maestro Cinetik

notes.title: United Front (large content and feature update)
notes.content:
Dear players,

I am pleased to announce a fantastic new update! Playtesters were highly satisfied with it, so I believe you will love it too!

The main contents of this update are:

[list]
[*]A better (by far) automation system
[*]A large new scenario set in 1923, called United Front
[*]A difficulty system reworked and balanced (thanks to 1 month of playtests)
[/list]

[h3]A better (by far) automation system[/h3]

Tired of repetitive actions? Bored with province development? Overwhelmed by managing a large empire?

Just delegate these tasks to the AI!
In fact, you're not delegating tasks directly to the AI, but whole characters management.
While this feature existed previously, it has been enhanced and expanded.

[u]What as changed?[/u]

1) Now, you can delegate even your active characters to the AI. This can be reverted at any time, and if the AI hasn't utilized all of a character's QI, you can still utilize them during your turn to complete actions with the remaining QI.

2) The loyalty cost of delegating a character to the AI has been significantly reduced, so you no longer need to worry about using this feature.

3) You can still delegate characters from your reserve pool to the AI, which is essential for managing large multi-province domains. However, I've introduced two useful improvements.
(For those new to the game, the option to delegate characters from your reserve pool to the AI unlocks when you have 5 active characters.)

You can now assign these characters to specific provinces. These characters will appear in the province HQ panel, allowing you to interact with them directly. Additionally, I've implemented actions to facilitate the transfer of resources to them effortlessly.

[u]How to decide what kind of action the AI should perform?[/u]

The behavior of characters when controlled by the AI depends entirely on their roles. I invite you to read this[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3237756654] Steam guide about roles[/url].

If you aim for province development, employ a statesman character. For combating banditry, deploy a police character, and so on.

A warlord character will prioritize cultivating opium and building the largest army imaginable.

[u]How competent is the AI?[/u]

The AI's competence level is decent. 
Playtesters were generally satisfied with it. 
However, it's worth noting that I deliberately toned down its capabilities to ensure it doesn't match the opponent's AI. 
Additionally, characters in the reserve pool will exhibit less responsiveness compared to your active characters when delegated to the AI.


[h3]United Front scenario[/h3]

The new scenario spans from Sun Yat Sen's return to Guangzhou in 1923 until his death in 1925. Key events of this scenario include:

-The Beijing-Hankow railway strike
-The formation of the United Front between the Guomindang and the Communists
-The establishment of the Whampoa Academy and the presence of Soviet advisors in Guangzhou
-A merchant uprising in Guangzhou
-Conflict between Jiangsu and Zhejiang over control of Shanghai
-A new Zhili-Fengtian war leading to the collapse of the Zhili clique
-Feng Yuxiang's betrayal and the formation of the Guominjun

The Communist, Guomindang, and Zhili Clique factions are central to many events and dialogues in the scenario.

The Zhili Clique prompted me to extensively rework the automation system. Playtesters found managing large factions remarkably easy with the new system.

Navigating the challenges of holding together a large faction at its peak power and on the brink of collapse offers an engaging challenge. If you've ever been hesitant to choose a large faction, now is the perfect opportunity to do so.

Furthermore, the introduction of a new significant scenario necessitated adjustments to opponent AI. They should now be more proficient, especially those specialized in combating Communists in 1927. However, I'll rely on your feedback for further fine-tuning, as they may require additional playtesting.

[h3]Difficulty sytem[/h3]

I recently introduced a difficulty system, and after weeks of playtesting, I made some slight improvements to it. 

There are now five different difficulty levels:

[u]Green[/u]: Designed for a relaxing game experience. Bandit generation has been reduced, and the maintenance cost of your armies is decreased.

[u]Seasonned / normal[/u]: he default difficulty level, perfect for playing as a small warlord in the warlords melee.

[u]Elite[/u]: The AI will field larger armies, reflecting historical accuracy. This level offers a challenging gameplay experience, particularly when playing as a major faction competing with other major cliques. It's also the difficulty level used for playtesting the game.

[u]Dare death[/u]: The AI will deploy even larger armies and may receive bonus resources at times.

[u]Generalissimo[/u]: At this level, you'll really notice the AI's advantage with bonus resources. 
It's intended for seasoned players seeking an extra challenge.


[h3]Next steps[/h3]

After such a big update, I will probably take a time to rest, coding smaller and more relaxing features.

In the to do list for next months (this is not an ordered list): 

-Some more 1927 content.
-Some more guides and wiki entries
-Steam achievements
-Linking the event chains of the different scenarios
-A 1923 sandbox? (if you really need it)
 

Have fun!

Post Scriptum: 
Don't hesitate to leave a comment below. Your feedback encourages us to keep improving the game, and we're excited to hear from you!

notes.title: Difficulty levels & new cheat codes
notes.content:
Hello,

The work on the 1923 scenario is progressing smoothly, and I am correcting bugs and adding features along the way. When I have cool stuff that can be published before the next content patch, I will release small updates like this one.

Today's update only applies to the Windows version. Versions for Linux and Mac will follow later.

[h1]Today's Update:[/h1]

[b]Difficulty Levels[/b]

You can now select a difficulty level when you launch a scenario. There are four difficulty levels:

[u]Green Difficulty Level[/u]:
This is the default difficulty level. It is perfect for playing as an underdog faction or for discovering the game.

[u]Seasoned Difficulty Level[/u]:
This difficulty level is intended to raise the challenge when you play as one of the major factions. Your opponents will be able to grow and maintain larger armies.

[u]Elite Difficulty Level[/u]:
Not only will your opponents be able to grow and maintain larger armies, but the game will also shamelessly cheat by giving random resources each turn to characters controlled by your opponents.

[u]Dare Death Difficulty Level[/u]:
Not only will your opponents get all the bonuses of the Elite difficulty levels, but your troops will also have a malus at their morale checks during fights.

[b]New Cheat Codes[/b]

"endwar" will disband a unit.
"flowerpower" will send all weapons of the selected unit into your faction stockpile.
"oneguntwoarms" will send rifles from the selected unit, but will leave 1 rifle per man (if there are enough guns).

For those new to the game: just press the "c" key to open the cheat console.

[b]Annoying Bug Fixed[/b]

You won't be able to use [enter] to trigger the action buttons anymore. That will prevent a free multiple action exploit.

I hope you will have a lot of fun playing with this update. I also need your feedback about the difficulty setting, as it certainly needs balance.

Maestro Cinetik

The Fengtian Clique's challenges will focus on:

-Enhancing their supply and industrial capabilities.
-Seeking revenge on the Zhili Clique.


The additional content for 1927 will revolve around new strategies to establish Red Bases, following the VIth Congress of the Chinese Communist Party. Given the Communist faction's lack of statesman characters, these new actions will offer opportunities to develop districts with peasant leaders and political workers. We'll also likely introduce more upgrades for the Communist armies and militias.

Enjoy!

Maestro Cinetik

notes.content:
Hello!

A new big update full of content is now online!

[list]

[/list]

[h2]New Scenario: 1927 Red Bases[/h2]

The new scenario features the entirety of China, except for Mongolia, and commences in August 1927. Anticipate numerous communist uprisings!

[b][u]The new scenario introduces new actions and abilities for the Communist player:[/u][/b]

Red Guards: A novel type of unit geared towards guerrilla actions.
An uprising mode for Guangzhou.
Long marches.
A plethora of new CCP historical characters, some with a military background.
Now, you'll truly be capable of establishing robust red bases and defending them. Playtests have demonstrated that seasoned players can assume control over multiple provinces.
When playing as the CCP, you can select your initial faction: will you lead the Nanchang uprising, the Harvest uprising, or the Hailufeng Soviet?

[b][u]New abilities for the Guomindang:[/u][/b]

In this scenario, you govern a new entity: the Nanjing government. Your mission is to both conclude the Northern Expedition and reunify the Party, currently fragmented into several factions.

You may consider dismissing your Generalissimo, Jiang Jieshi, to facilitate the Party's reunification. If you do so, he will return even more potent later on.

With a perpetual need for funds, you gain new actions for government control of the opium market (they become available after developing the anti-smuggling brigade in a district).

[b][u]New abilities for the Fengtian/Anguojun:[/u][/b]

The Northern warlords have coalesced into the Anguojun and, at the scenario's inception, are launching a final (perhaps desperate) counter-offensive.

You'll need to manage your currency printing: as long as you continue to gain ground, all will be well, but any setbacks may result in the devaluation of your currency.

The Japanese are no longer as friendly as they once were and aspire to seize control of Manchuria. If you begin to lose ground and your relations deteriorate, they might even plot your assassination!

This faction also gains new actions for relocating peasants from the central plains of China to Manchuria and enjoys a special logistical bonus for supplying any unit connected by rail to the Mukden industrial complex.


[h2]Quality of Life Features[/h2]

Many enhancements have been incorporated, addressing numerous inconveniences.

Take a look at the options menu while in-game: you can now adjust settings such as disabling the automatic display of district reports or displaying area control colors on the map regardless of the zoom level.

Managing large factions has been made significantly more convenient with a new feature: you now have the option to delegate a character from your reserve pool to the AI. Such a character will act autonomously, utilizing their best abilities based on their roles. This option becomes available once you have a minimum of five characters in your active pool.

To simplify navigation between provinces, I've added buttons throughout the province map.

Additionally, you'll notice new buttons in the upper-right corner of character sheets for smoother interactions with your characters.

And for added convenience, you can now press "P" to instantly open the province map for the selected character's current location.

[h2]New Cheat Codes[/h2]

You're in for a treat with the second one!

**[b]"miamivice"[/b]: Grants you anti-smuggling brigades and opium suppression offices in every district under your control.

**[b]"thepartyneverends"[/b]: Extends the game's duration by an additional 100 turns.

**[b]"cantonragtime"[/b]: Originally intended for playtesting purposes only, this cheat code may produce unexpected results if used in the wrong scenario or with the wrong faction. It triggers the 1927 Guangzhou Uprising. Use with caution!

[h2]What's Next[/h2]

It seems like it's time to start working on a better wiki.

On the to-do list, we have:

-Adding new music tracks to the game.
-Expanding "Guangdong Revolutionary Base" and "1925 Sandbox scenarios" to encompass all of China.
-Introducing a "Shanghai" Communist group to the 1927 Red Bases scenario.
-Creating a 1927 sandbox scenario.
-Incorporating more spy/underground life-specific actions and Red base organization actions into the "1927 sandbox."
-Expanding the People's Liberation Army (PLA) with additional abilities, such as the ability to change commanders at will.
-Pursuing the translation into Simplified Chinese.*

Please share in the comments which of these developments excites you the most.

Maestro Cinetik

*It still progresses, but expect some delays, including the fact that the new patch alone introduced tons of new texts.

notes.title: 1927 Red Bases preview
notes.content:
It's incredible how quickly time passes when you're working hard on a game! A player recently informed me that I haven't posted any news for over a month. So, here's a preview of my current work.

A significant content and quality of life update is in progress. I've included some images below for you to take a look at. I don't have a specific ETA yet, but it's about 80% complete.

What's included?

[h3]1927 Red Bases[/h3]

Red Bases will be an extensive scenario covering the entire China map (excluding Mongolia). I want it to be the equivalent of the Little Model China sandbox scenario, but set in the late 1920s.

The scenario begins with the Nanchang uprising, a divided nationalist faction, and Northern Warlords poised to launch a violent counter-offensive.

Certain parts of the game have been reworked specifically to simulate the Communist Party's evolution towards guerrilla warfare. Expect new gameplay mechanics.

To reflect the turmoil of the White Terror and the difficulty in communication between the Party Central Committee and the various provinces, the CCP faction is divided into four groups, each with its own victory conditions. Of course, you will be able to join forces with the other groups and reunite them.

Two new governments have been added: the Anguo military government in Beijing and the Nanjing government.

The Guomindang itself is divided into several factions (The Nanjing faction, Tang Shengzhi in Hubei, and Wang Jingwei).

There are many other exciting features coming with this scenario, but I'll let you discover them when it's released.

[h3]Quality of Life Features[/h3]

Many more options, including:

[b]The possibility to let an AI control characters in your reserve pool[/b]
This option will unlock when you recruit your fifth character. It will help you grow a large faction. Keep in mind that characters controlled by the AI won't be as loyal or efficient as you might hope.

[b]Move on right-click option[/b]
This feature is designed to prevent misclicks. I'm not entirely sure if I like it, but it's now available in the options menu.

[b]Do not automatically open reports[/b]
You can now toggle this option in the menu. I know it has been a source of annoyance for some of you.

[b]More consistent map information at any zoom level[/b]
The system that displayed different information depending on the zoom level was not popular. Now, you can even keep the colored controlled areas visible on the map at maximum zoom levels if you prefer.

[b]Improved navigation between provinces[/b]
I've made it easier to navigate between provinces on the province maps.

I'm sure I've forgotten to mention some of the features I'm working on these days, but you'll discover them in due time.

If you have any bright ideas or requests, please feel free to share them using the comment section.

Have fun!

notes.title: Chinese players feedback update - October update
notes.content:
Hello!

As you know, I will keep adding content to Rise of the White Sun (until you all get bored by the game^^)
And you have your word to say: the poll about the next big content patch is still open [url=https://strawpoll.com/NPgxEvqGAZ2]here[/url] 

[h1]This first October patch is a Chines players feedback update.[/h1]

I made a selection of things to improve from the many feedbacks Chinese have provided these last weeks, and put the result in this update.

Main topics:

[list]
[*]The Chinese Communist Party in the 1920 scenarios
[*]The military actions for the Chinese Communist Party in the 1920 scenarios
[*]Dealing with bandits and disasters
[*]The Chinese Translation
[/list]

[h2]The Chinese Communist Party in the 1920 scenarios[/h2]

From your feedbacks, I learned that many of you were confused by the fact the Communist players also controls the Mongolian People's Party.
This was because in the developer's intent it was a Comintern faction, not a Chinese Communist Party faction.
That was not clear, and the desire to play the Communist Party alone totally understandable.

==>You can now play the Communist Party in the 1920 scenarios without bothering about Mongolia and White Russians

You can still play as the Comintern if you prefer (because some players prefered it that way). 

[h2]Military actions for the Chinese Communist Party in the 1920 scenarios[/h2]

Many of you asked for military features for the Communists that are more "1927 and beyond" related.
But, well, ...why not!
I want to keep the game the most historical possible, so, turning your 1920 students into seasonned guerilla warriors will be done by using cheatcodes to unlock contents that are available later in the game.

Here are some new cheat codes:

"downwithlandlords": will unlock useful actions, to raise peasant armies, proclaim soviets and punish landlords

"redarmy": will add 3 historical officer characters to your characters reserve pool (if you are playing in 1920)

"1927mao": will unlock an event to turn young 1920 Mao into a peasant guerilla leader

And an old useful cheatcode:

"redsu": will launch a communist uprising in Shanghai (you will need to control pickets, if you don't want to lose it immediately)


[h2]Dealing with bandits and disasters[/h2]

Some of you had trouble dealing with bandit and disasters. 
Others had many questions about province management.

I added a province management "practice scenario" set in Shanxi. 
This is not exactly a tutorial, but a scenario with far more turns that needed, and no warlord opponent.
So you can take your time to experiment.

Many help panels will be displayed during this scenario answering the FAQ related to province management, bandits and disasters.

Tell me if that new kind of scenario is useful or enjoyable for you.
You can also answer this Steam news to request such scenarios to explore other topics.

[h2]The Chinese translation[/h2]

Here I need to apologize to the translation team.
I thought that using a robot translation to let players test the game until the translation was complete would be a pleasant surprise.

I believed the disclaimers and explanations both on the Steam page and in game would have been explicit, but some players blamed the translators for the poor Robot translation. 

I, the dev, did it because I needed to kill the many bugs created by the Chinese localisation, and decided that it could be cool to make it available, instead of keeping it to myself.

Here is how it works from a dev point of view:

1)The game will fetch the translation made by the human team.
2) If that part of the text is not translated yet, it will then display the robot translation
3) If no text is found, the English translation is then used
4) If there is no English translation, a text will be displayed to report the missing variable to the dev

I was really proud of that cascade system.

I hope you will understand and be patient.

If you want to participate to the translation effort, you can just answer to this news. 

Please don't use the answer to promote your paid translations services, because there is so much text that even with low costs and poor quality results if would cost more than the game will ever earn.

notes.title: Sandbox Scenario new content

[h2]New Characters' actions[/h2]

I plan to add many more actions, but for the moment, you have that 3 new actions available from the Character's interaction window:

[u]Indulge[/u]: two characters with the playboy role may become real life friends with this action!

[u]Political networking[/u]: Your diplomat and statesman characters will gain a real influence when using this action. It is useful to shape your diplomatic operations. It is perfect as a preparatory action before taking over a government or issuing a circular telegram.

Some warlords AI and Ma QI AI have been reworked to make them last longer in the sandbox mode.
As it is in test phase, only few of the warlords have this new AI.

In a sandbox mode, using cheat code is more a way to explore the game than to really cheat, isn't it?
These cheat codes have all been created to test the code.

"punksinpekin": will reinforce the Police in Beijing and check for a revolt (You will see nothing happening if you have strong garrison there)

"angrylama": just watch the monks rebelling in Xikang, because... why not?

"choekyinyima": Adds the Panchen Lama to your character's pool

"grigorisemenov": Adds a famous White Russian Cossack Ataman to your character's pool

"puyi": Guess which famous historical character that code will add to your pool?

"tycoon": Speeds up all your policies development

"yollo": That one will give max resources to all your characters (quite powerful)

"wearefamily": Will boost to the maximum the loyalty of your characters

"Bogdbreaksfree": Will clean Urga from units and set it neutral

[h2]Some more treason[/h2]

Imagine you have many province capitals under your control: do you really imagine that garrison commanders won't start dreaming of a governor's career? 
If you have too many armies, the control over them will losen, I you may have some nasty surprise from time to time.

[h2]Chinese integration tests[/h2]
正在进行中，但还有很多文本需要翻译
You can click on the Chinese language button to test it.
You will see that most of the scenario and landing page texts have not been translated yet.

I will add new texts from time to time as they become translated.

Well, I hope you will have fun with this new content,

Maestro Cinetik

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/a78d0787af718eff1829da2833a872cba67ce6e3.png[/img]

[b]September 1920,[/b]

Xinjiang governor Yang Zengxin is worried.
The Russian Civil War has direct repercussions over his province: White Russians armed bands are using China as a rear base to conduct vengeful raids into Bolshevik territories.
Since the fall of Yuan Shikai, Yang Zengxin has not received any funds, nor any modern weapon for his army...
It seems that the governor is on his own to deal with his powerful and wild unwelcome Russian guests.

The governor's enemies in Xinjiang and Beijing are awaiting an error to interfer in his business and oust him from power.
Soon the Red Army will be tempted to in turn cross the border to eradicate the last White armies.

As governor Yang, you have 103 turns to get rid of your enemies in Xinjiang. 

To recreate Xinjiang and Gansu, new types of districts have been created for the game: oasis towns and khanates. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/c8921c8591cef099c77025b44952a4768af15a06.png[/img]

[b]Some More Russian Civil War action![/b]

To better simulate the last actions of the Russian civil war, many features have been added: raids into Bolshevik territory, the possibility to recruit White Russians stragglers, the possibility to use the lasts Imperial Russian consulates in Xinjiang to help you... 

All the White Russians commanders in Xinjiang are in the game: Dutov, Annenkov, Bakich, but be ready to lose them to treachery and assassinates. 

As the White Russian player, You are not the only Russians in town: Bolshevik agents can bevery active in the area!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/1f539d6311ae3216c4021a6adaa3b670a7b74526.png[/img]

[b]We are family![/b]

Most of you know or have eard of Ma Bufang, but they were many more Ma in town at that time.
Playing in Gansu have many similarities with the Sichuan gameplay: a lot of factions on a single territory, but with more desert, more horses and ridiculously small armies (by Guangdong standards).

September 1920,

the Hui warlords in Gansu resent the rule of the overnor Zhang Guangjian and petitioned Beijing for his replacement, arguing that Gansu should be governed by people from Gansu.

However, the situation is not as simple, as the province is divided into eight military districts, with half being governed by a Hui commander and the other half by Han commanders.

The Han population is still unwilling to accept the idea of a Hui governor due to the frightening memory of past Hui rebellions.
The situation remained at a standstill until Zhang Guangjian lost support in Beijing, as the power of the Anhui Clique collapsed under attacks from the Zhili and Fengtian Cliques.

Zhang Guangjian's days as a governor are numbered, and the question arises as to who will rise as the next strong leader in Gansu.

You have 103 turns to impose your rule in Gansu and its surrounding areas.

The Ma factions will receive more love and special features in the next patch (Tibet)

Have Fun!

notes.title: Spirit Soldiers!
notes.content:
Many cool new things in the last patch:

-An army list screen reworked toi manage all your armies easily from one screen
-The Little Model China scenario has been extended to include Hubei, Henan and Shaanxi
-6 new factions and 14 new characters
-Many AI have been reworked
-Some new events added
-Some bugs killed...

But the most interesting addition in my opinion is a new type of faction:

[h2]The Spirit Soldiers[/h2]

Did you ever dream of playing as a mystical sect, whose aim is to defend the peasants against bandits and rapacious warlords?

That dream came true!

You certainly encountered these guys before as a neutral faction in Guizhou.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/8850846619ef1dd69d046d120b474f1e912172cd.png[/img]

The spirit soldiers have distinct game mechanisms and actions. 

[b][u]Gain Magical Immunity to bullets and other battle charms[/u][/b]

Spirit Soldiers units can be trained to gain magical powers (not for real, but it has a real impact if you believe in them).
It is possible to maintain areally high morale and loyalty level among Spirit Soldiers, through magical ceremonies and superstition.

Bullets and rifles are not your kind of weapons: don't expect to inflict the same huge damages as Northern Warlords armies do. 
Yes, Spirit Soldiers have a bonus to hand to hand fighting, as they master the sword and the spear, but let's be honest, that will never match the damages of artillery fire. 

[b][u]Raise impressive armies of peasants in no time[/u][/b]

Spirit Soldiers are able to summon impressive troops of peasants.
The only drawback is that these gatherings are temporary (they last 1 turn before disbanding).
Also, they have the same problem as any other peasant troops: they tend to vanish as they venture far from their home village. 

[b][u]Like fish in the sea[/u][/b]

Spirit Soldiers troops have bonus to ambush their opponents, and to their supplying capacity if they are in a friendly district.
Playing as this faction, most of the time, you won't have to worry about supplying your troops.

[b][u]Ages old feuds[/u][/b]

As you extend your influence in nearby districts, you will certainly face rival secret societies, and struggle to maintain your sphere of influence.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/cf3b2ece76880d16f810c82fe24bd5567175807e.png[/img]

[h2]Next steps[/h2]

[b][u]Short Term[/u][/b]

I will now spend some time on some small but nice features, like adding special actions for Feng Yuxiang, the christian general, or some more content to the Old vs Young Guizhou Cliques.

Then I will go for something bigger:

What about a scenario about the 1927 CCP soviets and uprisings?

 [b][u]Medium term[/u][/b]

The "Little Model China" and "Guangdong  Revolutionary Base"  scenario will be extended.
"Little Model China" will include most of China provinces.

The "Shanghai Uprising" scenario will certainly be reworked.

[h2]Interacting with Foreign Powers[/h2]

A lot of new actions have been added to buy weapons or borrow money from Foreign colonial empires.
That won't come for free: you will certainly have to sell away some sovereignty to benefit from foreign aid.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/e905b997e3d5fe5a443313b9041d68d512d2e92a.png[/img]

The relationship of your faction with each Foreign Power is the main variable here. As your relationship increases, you will unlock new actions.
But beware! 
Colonial Powers are competing with each other and you can't befriend everybody.
Worst: Chinese patriots won't be kind with traitors and you may earn the infamous title of "running dog of Foreign Imperialism".



[u]Soviet-British power play in Guangdong[/u]

The Soviet will support the GMD and the CPC to organize a boycott against British held Hong Kong, ruining its economy.
Local warlords will have there a unic occasion to gain the British Empire friendship by supplying goods to Hong Kong.
The British will search for some able faction to counter the GMD and end the strike, providing it with $ and rifles.

All that is now in the game!

The CPC AI has been reworked so the strike can get really damaging to Hong Kong.
If ever the Guangzhou is taken by a warlord faction, the strike would immediately end.


[h2]Southern Guangdong faction reworked[/h2]

There is a nice not well known faction in Southern Guangdong. It has been reworked with added events, and more characters (they are 3 now).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/bbf66a5c294e062e885c71bee48169362b1fd7e0.png[/img]

That faction controlled Hainan, so the island has been added in the game as a new province. 
A starting event will give you an opportunity to influence the game to suits your playing style.


[h2]New characters[/h2]

[u]The Southern faction[/u] gained two characters including one with a bandit background. 
Those of you who have already used bandits characters from the Old Guangxi Clique know how useful they can be.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/ac50e3bae1ea9edb47045fc40661be089b59ca16.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/7e7863b1081ae85de4bd32e366d4952104a3f9d0.png[/img]

[u]The Guizhou Clique[/u] faction leader is currently fighting in Sichuan. He is now in Guizhou characters pool.
It won't be easy to gather enough face to have him back. But with the generalissimo/overlord role, he will certainly boost your faction effectiveness at fighting bandits and enlarging your domain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/cbedf95f9b943b292db2e88a6b28fc1ca6809d30.png[/img]

[u]The Guomindang[/u] was not lacking characters, but some important figures were still missing.
Tan Yankai is a very able character you can use in mist of your strategies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/2c85abdfb615d8974a23ad670c8d5f3e68fd39b9.png[/img]


[h2]中文[/h2]

You have been many to ask for a chinese version of the game.
You will be pleased to learn that the translation into chinese by community has started.
This is a long process: there is as much text as there would be in a big book.
So be patient.
We have done it before for Cauldrons of War Stalingrad, so we know this is an efficient way to have a great quality translation. Efforts are coordinated from the Discord: you can join if you are both fluent in Chinese and in English.
A profesional translation would have been totally out of reach of a small indie dev (And it would have costed more than this game would ever earn), community translation is the only way to do it while fact checking history and quality.


[h2]What's next?[/h2]

Next on the poll was the scenario opening of the Northern Expedition in Hunan. So Hunan will be included in the next content patch.

I will also pursue the deepening of the Guangdong Revolutionary base scenario.

[u]Answer this news to tell me which faction I should rework now[/u]: 
-Chen Jiongming (with Anarchist inspired policies and army actions, and relationship with the merchants and the gentry special events)
-The Yunnan Clique (with some Opium stuff, and tribal minorities)
 
[h2]Boring List of killed bugs and reworked features [/h2]

-Save files have been cleaned: no more living dead armies coming back while you have destroyed them.
-Saved files: no more events popping endlessly after loading
-Characters limit: now that's 7 characters and no more!
-AIs: most of the AIs have been reworked. 
-Tons of typos have been corrected (You read the texts, don't you?)
-The "alt" shortcut to display the numbers of actions on the map works fine now
-Non CPC factions can no more send back Borodin to Moscow!
(CPC faction can still do it, and that may be useful to reclaim a free character slot to recruit some more relevant character)

Add to that bugs nobody reported and those cleared in the previous patches and you have now a pretty decent build. 

I hope this news was not too lenghty :)

[b]Have fun![/b]

Maestro Cinetik

notes.title: Warlord factions : new scenario in the demo
notes.content:
May 1924

Guangxi, although a very poor province, is coveted by its powerful neighbors to the North, West and East.
Lu Rongting, the current governor, has not been able to make sufficiently powerful allies and his power is contested by a new clique from Guangxi won over to the republican ideals of Sun Yat Sen.
Arriving from Hunan, General Shen Hongying, supported by the powerful warlord Wu Peifu, also claimed the province.
Which faction will rule Guangxi? 
Only the results of bloody fights and bold treasons will tell.
You have 23 turns to take control of the whole province with your faction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/d554ab5c9d3fdac4a583b81d91dcc4ca525bee8c.png[/img]

[h1]Play as the Old Guangxi Clique[/h1]

This faction has some real weaknesses but also some unsuspected strengths.

Usually, corruption, fraud and smuggling will be very high in the districts controled by this faction. 
This can be partly fixed by policies to fight corruption like training the magistrates.

Old Guangxi clique leaders  have strong local ties: they can use their strong relationships among the Zhuang ethnie to quickly raise irregular armies. It can be done with the action "Zhuang Self Government". use it wisely because this action will also strongly reduce your income.

If you play with this faction, don't forget that your characters are former bandits!
They go along very well with smugglers and bandits. These sympathies give them bonuses for actions like "smuggling rifles" or "recruit bandits". 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41622060/97a3d18fb15c87b129e57f9531f10db25922fe0e.png[/img]

[h1]Play as the New Guangxi Clique[/h1]

This faction has some real strengths and no real weaknesses.
The New Guangxi Clique  has a unique combination of complementary and useful characters. 
LiZongren and Bai Chongxi are very competent strategists while Huang Shaohong will be perfect as Civil Governor.
If you play this faction, your army can be organized on the nationalist model.
The Chinese Nationalist Republic you support is trained and organized by soviet advisors. This gives you many more organizational actions than your enemies. Try to create a "Political Department" in each of your armies as soon as you can, it will unlock other useful actions to make your armies more efficient.

[h1]Cool things you will do in this scenario include:[/h1]

-Bribing enemy armies

If you play it, I would love to have your feedback!

Have fun!

notes.title: PLAY THE DEMO!
notes.content:
December 1926: the victorious National Revolutionary Army commanded by Bai Chongxi is approaching Shanghai where CCP and GMD agents are busy planning an uprising. Behind the scenes, high-ranking warlord officers are negotiating a comfortable future for themselves in exchange for betraying their masters while Jiang Jieshi is plotting with the Green Gang to get rid of his communist allies.

This is a time of dishonest plots and brutal action.

[b]Revolution needs serious skills, are you up to the task?[/b]
==> [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1189100/Rise_Of_The_White_Sun/]Download the demo and check it out![/url]


[h2]IMPORTANT THINGS TO KNOW[/h2]
Don't expect to be able to jump right into this game without effort.
The uprising mechanics may be new to some of you, and the historical situation depicted is very complex, so you won't escape reading texts and tooltips if you want to understand what is going on.

Also, the scope of possible actions in the game is wide. 
During your first attempt, you may feel overwhelmed in the sea of possibilities.
Don't worry, and just try things to explore the game.

[b]Your efforts will be rewarded by a unique experience[/b]

The content of the Demo is very limited and focuses on Uprising management.
As the Chinese Communist Party, you will plan the Shanghai Uprising, take over the city and try to survive to the political split with the GMD.
[b]This is enough to be an uprising simulator stand alone[/b], ...but not enough to grasp the whole game experience.

[b]Content of the Demo:[/b]
-1 scenario (The Shanghai Uprising), 
-1 playable faction (The Chinese Communist Party)
-The world is limited to the city of Shanghai

[b]These parts of the game are NOT featured in this Demo (but will be in the complete game):[/b]
-Whole China playable
-All chinese factions playable
-Province management
-Military expeditions
-Factions management
-Multiplayer
-Save system

Have fun!

notes.title: Milestones & First Insights
notes.content:
So what can you expect and when?

[h2]The Shanghai Uprising Demo[/h2]
For the first Demo, we plan to unveil only a small part of the game system.
We've selected the Shanghai 1927 Uprising for its tense background and dramatic outcome.

[b]Imagine[/b]: 
The internal struggle and the communists and the different factions of the Guomindang is at its height as a powerful National Revolutionary Army approaches Shanghai. 
In the city itself, the warlord forces are quickly losing the support of the merchants and the working class is ready to launch an uprising to welcome the Revolutionary forces.
The Green Gang and the foreign powers are worrying for their business and ploting with every other faction to maintain their situation...

[b]That could be fun, don't you think so?[/b]

Such a demo won't display cool game mechanics like Province management, diplomacy or military expeditions, but [b]uprising planning[/b] is rich enough in the "Rise of the White Sun" system to be a game on its own, so we are sure you will have fun.

That demo will be multiplayer, so you can team with friends to overthrow the warlord.

When? Well... we are progressing fast, so I would say january or February 2022.


==> [url=https://riseofthewhitesun.com/index.php/2021/11/12/game-the-shanghai-insurrection-march-april-1927-part-1/]More on that on our blog[/url]


[h2]The eary access for June (hopefully)[/h2]

What can you expect in the early access?
We plan to deliver the 1926-1929 years, simulating the whole northern expedition. You would be able to play with most of the warlords, the GMD and the Communists.
Province management, military operations, diplomacy, uprisings and subversive activities... All that will be in the game by then.

While in early access, we plan to add (may be not in this order):
-the 1925 Hong Kong strikes
-the warlord wars prior and after the Northern Expedition
The maximum period we will eventually cover is 1911-1949 (that only if enough players are interested by the game) and the minimum one is 1925-1931.
